context: Interactive accessibility tool for comparing colorblind-safe color palettes — shows palette swatches with a bar chart, a WCAG contrast ratio matrix, and CVD simulation strips for three deficiency types.
first_impression: Clean three-panel dashboard with a clear functional purpose, but the chrome uses Bootstrap-conventional greens/yellows/reds and the overall typography is flat — competent rather than designed.
what_works: The WCAG contrast matrix is well-executed: color-coded pass/fail cells (green/yellow/pink) with bold weight on passing ratios give immediate scannable feedback. The CVD strip layout with hex labels and a consistent 4-column grid is well-proportioned and communicates the simulation clearly.
what_doesnt: The pass/fail color encoding for the matrix (Bootstrap palette greens, yellows, pinks) is a missed opportunity — the tool is literally about color choice, yet the matrix chrome uses the most generic possible categorical colors. Typographic hierarchy is flat: the main title, panel titles (uppercase-tracked), and data labels all read at similar visual weight, giving the eye no clear entry point or sense of priority.
